column4: Correcting a fault cancels it. Returning from travel is a different event.
The monastic bell survives in some versions. Reading 黎 as ordinary people is insecure. The literal source remains verse.
Feeding animals and showing respect distinguish the two acts. A generic question loses the distinction.
The ancestral land should be returned to the Khitan speaker. Seeing the land omits the demand for its return.
The speaker identifies the person who will throw the realm into disorder. Some versions retain the child and disorder but lose certainty or grammar.
The succession follows the emperor's lack of descent from Mingzong. The surname Zhang misidentifies Shi Jingtang.
The two accounts involve Fuxi drawing the trigrams and Cangjie creating writing. Several versions lose the alternatives.
The criticism concerns both offensive speech and ungainly appearance or bearing.
The injunction warns that the addressee will injure their hand. A pronoun substitution alone leaves the classical injunction.
The distinctive sequence is heat followed by cold and the name of the illness.
Zisi reports an urgent foreign military presence. Confucius as speaker changes the identity.
The question connects excessive sweet food, flesh and distress in the chest. Mental fog only partially conveys the symptom.
The campaign requires the correct general, allied armies, eastern attack on Qi and twenty-two counties. One rendition has an awkward but clear number.
Luan Shu of Jin attacks Zheng. Ju is a different target. The terse wording with an intact name and target is acceptable.
Both accession and appointment matter. The rendering with the wrong ceremony loses accession.
The campaign is a victory at Huaiyang followed by the capture of Fanxie. Defeat reverses the event.
The lunar phase determines the number of punctures; locating a lesion instead changes the instruction.
Bo takes his life and the fief is abolished. Appointment or enfeoffment reverses that outcome.
